title: Turn off Licensing
summary: The requirement cascade on Diceroll's Features page: turning off Licensing also turns off Commerce, which needs it. The dialog names every dependent with what stops for each, says what is kept, and that it records one change in Activity.
compare: The dialog opens over the Features page (dimmed, drawn as products.features) when the Licensing switch is pressed and before anything changes; Escape and Cancel leave both features on. With the dialog open the page can't scroll: on desktop the dialog is centred in the viewport (ui/Dialog.tsx).
The title names the feature and the product: 'Turn off Licensing for Diceroll?'. The lead line says why more turns off, once: 'Commerce needs Licensing, so it turns off too.'

Every feature that turns off is listed (kit .change-list), the one pressed first and then each dependent (transitively), each with its glyph, 'On → Off' on its title line and one sentence on what stops. The lead line already says why Commerce turns off, so its row carries no 'Needs Licensing' tag. Features that are already off (Cloud Sync) are not listed.

The Licensing lines say what players experience, one fact per line: 'Players keep playing for up to 30 days offline.' then 'Then no license confirms, Free tier included.' The reach is one meta line from the dry run: '11,239 devices checked a license in 30 days'.
The Commerce lines say what players notice, one fact per line: 'The game can't show its 4 offers.' and 'Purchases and restores are refused.'
Under the list, two lines with their glyphs: 'Data is kept.' and 'Undo from Activity turns both back on.'
Confirming records one change in Activity, not two, and its Undo turns both back on (the second line under the list).

The danger button says exactly what happens: 'Turn off Licensing and Commerce'. No typed confirmation. Cancel is the neutral outline button (visible in dark) and has focus when the dialog opens (EXPERIENCE.md confirmations).
The words are feature names only; no service slugs (license, commerce) and no 'capability'.

Phone: the dialog is the console's bottom sheet (kit .overlay.sheet: rounded top corners, drag handle, the body scrolling), the danger button full width above Cancel, and the 'On → Off' marks stay on each feature's title line. Desktop and tablet centre the dialog in the viewport (kit .overlay.center).

Pressed, the danger button reads 'Turning off…' with a spinner and both buttons are disabled. If it fails the dialog stays open with an inline error saying what went wrong and how to retry, and both features stay on (ADMIN.md §5.2).
This is a danger dialog because a dependent turns off and it reaches many devices; turning off a feature that nothing needs is a caution dialog (L1) with its consequences.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Masthead mark (B4): from 1024px a 48px flat tile on this page (the feature's glyph on a landing page, the product's icon on a product page) replaces the orientation chip; below 1024 the chip carries the context; never on a dense data page, a record or a state page.

Dialog and drawer head (B4): a 3px rule in the origin's accent along the top (none on a destructive or cautious confirmation), a head band with a hairline, one leading glyph or none (severity on a confirmation, the subject's mark on a record, never a service tile), title at or under 20/28; blurred backdrop with a flat fallback under reduced transparency.
Destructive head (admin-1-20): the danger glyph only, no rule and no tile; Cancel keeps initial focus; copy stays the terse multi-review version.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the Licensing line now says what players experience, the dialog is centred on desktop and a bottom sheet on phone, and Cancel is visible in dark.

findings.issue: The Licensing line said the game can't activate or refresh a license but never said what players experience: whether activated copies keep running offline, for how long, and whether Free-tier players are locked out.
findings.resolution: Rewritten from the SDK gate's offline grace (client-core gate.ts runs a cached license until graceUntil): 'Players already activated keep playing until their offline window ends, up to 30 days. After that, and on every new install, Diceroll can't confirm a license, Free tier included.' The 11,239 reach figure stays.

findings.issue: On phone the dialog was a top-anchored card, not the console's bottom sheet; on desktop it was top-anchored rather than centred; in dark Cancel's fill matched the dialog surface.
findings.resolution: With the dialog open the page no longer scrolls, so the render is the first viewport: centred on desktop, a bottom sheet on phone (rounded top corners, drag handle, safe-area padding, danger above Cancel). Cancel is an outline button. Lead: the kit's .overlay still top-anchors every dialog; a kit-wide sheet and centring would spare each screen this override.

findings.issue: 'Turning Licensing back on later doesn't turn Commerce back on' and 'Reverting this change turns both back on' read as contradicting each other; no busy or failure state; initial focus not stated.
findings.resolution: One sentence now: 'Turning Licensing back on with its switch leaves Commerce off; reverting this change in Activity turns both back on.' The audit meta says 'one entry for both'. Compare adds the busy label 'Turning off…', the inline error that keeps both features on, and initial focus on Cancel (shown focused in the render).

findings.issue: Cross-screen: the Features page under the dialog had per-service switch colours and 20 px phone switches.
findings.resolution: The page underneath follows products.features: console-accent switches, Packages, requirement marks, 44×24 switches on phone.

findings.issue: The Cancel focus ring was the loudest thing in the dialog; the same pair was named four times; the close X sat off the title's centre.
findings.resolution: The lead sentence is gone (the second row reads 'Needs Licensing'); the Licensing row reads 'Players keep playing up to 30 days offline, then Diceroll can't confirm any license (Free tier too).'; the footer is one line 'Data is kept. Undo from Activity turns both back on.'; the X lines up with the title; autofocus is removed so the ring shows only in an interaction state; 'On → Off' is a 12px faint red pill at 4.5:1; meta is 12px; on phone Cancel is a ghost button so the red action is the only emphasised one. The page behind now matches products.features.

findings.issue: Shorten to 'Turn off both', reverse the button order, remove the X on phone, highlight the Licensing row in the backdrop, reduce the blur.
findings.resolution: declined: The long label is the explicit one and matches the plan's destructive-action rule; button order is a kit convention; the backdrop and X are not spacing.

findings.issue: Draw pressed, failed and success frames and a toast with Undo.
findings.resolution: declined: New frames and components are a separate scope.
